title: Salmon Rice Bowls for the Crew

shortDescription: Roasted salmon with rice, cucumbers, and sesame dressing
subtitle: Roasted salmon with rice, cucumbers, and sesame dressing
description: Soy-glazed salmon, rice, cucumbers, avocado, and a sesame drizzle make a bright crew meal.

steps.title: Heat oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 400°F and line sheet pans so the salmon does not stick.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.instruction: Rinse sushi rice and cook it covered; do not lift the lid during the steaming time.

steps.title: Portion salmon
steps.instruction: Check fillets for pin bones and arrange them skin-side down with space between pieces.

steps.title: Glaze fish
steps.instruction: Brush salmon with soy, honey, and ginger glaze, saving clean glaze for the end.

steps.title: Roast salmon
steps.instruction: Roast until the thickest fillet flakes and reaches 145°F; avoid drying thin tail pieces.

steps.title: Slice cucumbers
steps.instruction: Slice cucumbers thinly and toss with rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Prepare avocado
steps.instruction: Cut avocado just before service and cover tightly so it does not brown.

steps.title: Finish glaze
steps.instruction: Simmer reserved untouched glaze for 1 minute, then brush a light coat over cooked salmon.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Keep cooked salmon covered above 140°F; never leave fish at room temperature.

steps.title: Build bowls
steps.instruction: Portion rice, salmon, cucumber, avocado, and sesame dressing into each bowl.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Salmon fillets — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Salmon fillets and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use frozen salmon thawed under refrigeration.
Keep skin on during roasting for easier handling.
tonightSpread: Condiments: sriracha mayo, nori strips, pickled ginger
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Salmon fillets in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Flake leftover salmon into fried rice.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The salmon roasts hands-off while rice and cold toppings are organized.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: mix dressing and slice vegetables 1 day ahead. Storage: refrigerate salmon 2 days. Reheating: reheat salmon to 165°F if serving hot leftovers.
